pending_commit.commit_message: BACKPORT: mwifiex: add support for FW memory read/write operations commit c2c6c85fca47f4c5ac99d482b64d59dbd142117c upstream This patch adds support for FW memory read/write operations via debugfs. This is useful during debugging FW issues. Examples: For reading FW memory location: echo r 0x01ac 0 > /sys/kernel/debug/mwifiex/mlan0/memrw cat /sys/kernel/debug/mwifiex/mlan0/memrw For writing FW memory location: echo w 0x01ac 0x55aa > /sys/kernel/debug/mwifiex/mlan0/memrw Signed-off-by: Chin-ran Lo <crlo@marvell.com> Signed-off-by: Cathy Luo <cluo@marvell.com> Signed-off-by: Avinash Patil <patila@marvell.com> Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org> Changes done in original commit 1) Allocated 3 bytes using memdup_user() instead of complete page 2) Used toupper() while matching user input 3) Replaced snprintf() with kasprintf() 4) removed redundant (void *) casting BUG=none TEST=Verified that reading and writing memory location is successful. Change-Id: I8eb24ff3458b2f40b987d1a2705a38fabfde3e0b Signed-off-by: Amitkumar Karwar <akarwar@marvell.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/296755 Reviewed-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/305578

BACKPORT: mwifiex: add prints debug ctrl support commit c687a0077faa0d24fe97a4434974f32bd359beb7 upstream This patch adds support for debugging print control in mwifiex driver. The debug level can be controlled via either by modules load parameter debug_mask or by writing to debug_mask in debugfs file. Signed-off-by: Zhaoyang Liu <liuzy@marvell.com> Signed-off-by: Cathy Luo <cluo@marvell.com> Signed-off-by: Avinash Patil <patila@marvell.com> Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org> Changes done in original commit 1) Removed redundant string "debug_mask=" displayed while reading debug_mask via debugfs command 2) Used kasprintf() to avoid whole page allocation BUG=none TEST=With this patch series applied, verified that appropriate logs can be enabled by changing debug level. Also, ran basic scan, connect and data path tests. CHROMIUM: mwifiex: corrections in PCIe event skb handling Preallocated event SKBs are getting reused for PCIe chipset. Their physical addresses are shared with firmware so that firmware can write data into them. This patch makes sure that SKB is cleared and length is set to default while submitting it to firmware. Signed-off-by: Amitkumar Karwar <akarwar@marvell.com> Signed-off-by: Zhaoyang Liu <liuzy@marvell.com> Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org> BUG=none TEST=With this patch series applied, verified that appropriate logs can be enabled by changing debug level. Also, ran basic scan, connect and data path tests. This patch fixes an issue caused by extra skb_trim() introduced by "mwifiex: add dump data debug support". The fix has been verfied on our reference setup(not chromebook). Change-Id: Id2d921427c3401843a4b51b96ea5630340e51b92 Signed-off-by: Amitkumar Karwar <akarwar@marvell.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/296759 Reviewed-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/305992

servod: inas: Add control map for INA calibration register. The calibration register for INAs that have it (219, 231) is currently manipulated by ina2xx driver but only in the direction of increased dynamic range at the expense of precision when current/power overflow. Re-calibrating in the other direction currently requires power-cycling the INAs. This can become an issue when user goes from reading cur/power for example in S0 to S5. Short-term fix is to add a control map (ina2xx.xml) such that user can at least forcibly recalibrate INA without power cycle. Signed-off-by: Todd Broch <tbroch@chromium.org> BUG=chrome-os-partner:45455 TEST=manual, start servod on favorite project w/ INAs wired. dut-control pp_vbat_ma pp_vbat_ma:1.23456 dut-control pp_vbat_cal_reg:recalibrate dut-control pp_vbat_ma pp_vbat_ma:1.23456 Change-Id: I5c4f480d0e7a4625e4d17424360d34a5e26b3ea0 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/301175 Commit-Ready: Todd Broch <tbroch@chromium.org> Tested-by: Todd Broch <tbroch@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Bryan Freed <bfreed@google.com>

futility: Revised support for RO+RW firmware The "rwsig" type is used for independent device firmware (not Chromebook BIOS) that need to verify themselves instead of using software sync. The expected use case is that a RO firmware contains a vb2_public_key struct along with an FMAP or other pointers to a slot for RW firmware. The RW firmware slot reserves room for a vb2_signature struct. This CL changes the args and behavior of the rwsig type, so that the RW firmware can be [re]signed independently of the rest of the image. BUG=chrome-os-partner:46254 BRANCH=smaug,ToT TEST=make runtests, manual Create a keypair: futility create --desc "Key One" tests/testkeys/key_rsa2048.pem foo Sign a RW binary and build a complete image out of the parts: futility sign --type rwsig --prikey foo.vbprik2 rw.bin sig.bin dd if=/dev/zero bs=65536 count=1 of=image.bin dd if=rw.bin of=image.bin conv=notrunc dd if=sig.bin bs=$((65536 - 1024)) seek=1 of=image.bin conv=notrunc Verify both the separate parts and the combined image: futility show --type rwsig --pubkey foo.vbpubk2 rw.bin sig.bin futility show --type rwsig --pubkey foo.vbpubk2 image.bin Re-sign the combined image with a different keypair: futility create --desc "Key Two" tests/testkeys/key_rsa1024.pem bar futility sign --type rwsig --prikey bar.vbprik2 image.bin Now the first key no longer verifies: futility show --type rwsig --pubkey foo.vbpubk2 image.bin But the second key does: futility show --type rwsig --pubkey bar.vbpubk2 image.bin Change-Id: Ifdddab08f218f506eb1dce28851b153d70140a7b Signed-off-by: Bill Richardson <wfrichar@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/305980 Tested-by: Vincent Palatin <vpalatin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Vincent Palatin <vpalatin@chromium.org>
